topic.title: Your rating was decided before your self-review
topic.claim: The self-appraisal you spent a weekend polishing is paperwork; your rating was fixed in a calibration meeting you weren't in.
topic.moment: Writing 'went above and beyond' in a portal at 11pm, two days before the deadline.

turn.believed: A strong self-review and good work decide your rating.
turn.actually: Each manager gets a fixed number of top ratings and argues for them in a closed room, usually before reading your form.

topic.because: The increment budget is set first and the bell curve has to fit it. Your form gives the decision something to point at.
topic.payoff: If your manager can't name what you did without opening your form, your rating was settled in that room.
topic.behaviour: Employees write long self-reviews; managers trade top ratings among themselves in calibration to fit a fixed curve.
topic.mechanism: A fixed raise budget needs a fixed number of winners, so the curve comes before the review.
topic.send_to: The teammate who is still editing their self-review at midnight.
topic.why_now: Appraisal season is coming, and people are about to over-invest in the wrong document.

score.why: The self-appraisal polished at 11pm is paperwork after a closed-room calibration; a relatable dark pattern.
